findings.message: The test for the zoned completion day passes a hand-set `completedDay: "2026-12-13"` into completedLine. It never goes through getRelease's new `releaseDay(entityZone(...), completed_at)`, which is where the fix actually is. If you delete the `completedDay:` line in queries.ts:345, completedLine falls back to the UTC day and this test still passes, because it supplies its own value. It also covers only one case. Fix: write a table-driven test that sets up projects whose legal entity is in a zone ahead of UTC, behind UTC, and with no entity (UTC). Complete each release with a deployment near midnight UTC through recordDeployment. Then assert getRelease(...).completedDay and the rendered 'Completed on … · Late/On time' line agree with `completion`.
findings.scenario: Remove `completedDay` from getRelease's return → the page shows the UTC day next to a zone-judged 'Late' again, and the test stays green.

findings.message: The shared missingForTracking predicate fixes a major, but its test covers one variant: category given, start missing. It has no table over the other partial sets (startDate only → category; targetDate only → category; category+startDate → targetDate). It also never checks that the card (proposeReleaseEdit) and the service (updateRelease) give the same answer for the same input, which is the point of the B4 fix. Fix: add a table-driven test that sends each partial set to both checkCardEdits and updateRelease and expects the same missing field and the same refusal.
findings.scenario: Change missingForTracking's field order or truthiness check → only the category-only case is tested, so a refusal on the wrong field for targetDate-only input is never caught.

findings.message: The completion day is now taken in the project's zone, but the same page still prints the voided completing deployment's day with the UTC `completedDay()` formatter. completedLine also keeps that UTC formatter as a fallback that the real read path never reaches, because getRelease always sets completedDay when completedAt is set. So the page has two rules for a release day. Fix: carry the zoned day for the void (or the zone) on the read and format it with releaseDay. Then remove the UTC fallback from completedLine.
findings.scenario: Project in Asia/Colombo; the completing deployment is voided at 2026-12-12T20:00Z → the note says 'voided on 12 Dec 2026', while the project's day is 13 Dec.

findings.message: The code no longer requires a name to start tracking a release. missingForTracking checks only category, start and target, and updateRelease falls back to the stored name or the version. But the README ('until `update_release` sets name, category and both dates together') and the update_release tool description (mcp.ts:127, 'needs its name, category and both dates together the first time') still say a name is required. The README also doesn't mention the new get_release_status_change read tool. Fix: update both texts so they match the code.

getStatusChange was inserted between getRelease and its doc comment. '/** One release with its proposals and full deployment history… */' now describes getStatusChange. Fix: move the comment back above getRelease and give getStatusChange its own.

The fix applies the project's time zone only to the 'Completed on' line. The UTC formatter `completedDay` is still there and is still used in two places. (1) It is the fallback inside `completedLine` when no zoned day was passed in. (2) In `ReleasePage.tsx:42` it prints the day the completing deployment was voided, in UTC, on the same page that now shows zoned days. So one page shows release dates under two different day rules. Fix: carry the zoned day for `completingVoided.at` on the read in `getRelease` (use `releaseDay` with the same zone). Delete the UTC `completedDay` formatter and the fallback in `completedLine`, so the only way to print a day is the zoned one.
findings.scenario: A project whose legal entity is in Australia/Sydney. Its completing deployment is voided at 2026-12-12T20:00Z, which is 13 Dec in Sydney. The banner says 'voided on 12 Dec 2026', while the completion and target days on the same page are Sydney days.
